title: The Speed, Cost and Thresholds of Reconfiguration
summary: Reconfiguration is not automatically better when it is faster, nor successful simply because it is cheap. Speed affects whether a system can learn and coordinate; cost affects whether transition can be sustained; thresholds mark when an older version can no longer carry reality on its own.

blocks.text: Reconfiguration is not automatically better when it is faster, nor successful simply because it is cheap. Speed affects whether a system can learn and coordinate; cost affects whether transition can be sustained; thresholds mark when an older version can no longer carry reality on its own.

These dimensions form an observation framework rather than a universal score. Systems have different buffers, substitutes and responsibilities, so the same pace or cost can produce different consequences.

This article uses only definitions and structural relations in the completed Book VI manuscript. Conceptual boundaries are not presented as additional historical facts, and no new causal claims are added beyond the manuscript.
